summary: Write Z = X + X^{m+1}W and induct on k, writing g = X·g̃ + g(0).

steps.claim: Z = X + X^{m+1}·W for some W.

Induction on k (for all g): write g = X·(shift of g) + g(0) and substitute Z; the terms of degree ≤ m + 1 coming from X^{m+1}W·(shift of g)(Z) are only W₀·g₁ at degree m + 1 when k = m + 1; the coefficient identity follows (simp, grind).
steps.lean:
induction k generalizing g <;> rw [g.eq_X_mul_shift_add_const, subst_add, subst_mul] <;> simp_all
    [add_mul, tsub_eq_zero_of_le, mul_assoc, coeff_X_pow_mul', le_of_succ_le, ← C.eq_def]; grind
